title: Per-pool throughput budget and hysteresis controller
author: Lena Fischer
description:
Motivation: recurring tenant oscillation and noisy redistribution of burst credits across dedicated pools have caused repeated transient SLA violations during back-to-back surges. This PR introduces a per-pool throughput budgeting abstraction plus a hysteresis controller that smooths admission decisions and prevents rapid open/close oscillations when headroom fluctuates.

Design summary: the controller maintains a moving-window budget for each pool (committed_throughput, soft_budget, expected_burn_rate) and exposes two key behaviors: (1) budget demultiplexing: incoming burst reservations are split into stable vs ephemeral tranches so long-lived reservations draw from a soft_budget while ephemeral spikes are served from a burst cache; (2) hysteresis gating: scale/admit decisions require a budget delta to exceed threshold for a configurable hold period before flipping state. Both behaviors are parameterized per-pool and per-tenant overrideable.

Config knobs added: per_pool.throughput_budget.initial_qps (int), per_pool.throughput_budget.window_seconds (int), per_pool.hysteresis.open_threshold_pct (float), per_pool.hysteresis.close_threshold_pct (float), per_pool.hysteresis.hold_seconds (int), admission.split_ratio (stable:burst). Defaults chosen to be conservative to avoid regressions.

Telemetry and alerts: new metrics exported under redwood_dedicated_pool_*: budget_available, budget_burn_rate, budget_forecast_p50_ms, hysteresis_state (0/1), recent_split_ratio. New alert: DedicatedPoolBudgetDepletion (fires when budget_available/pool < 5% for > 2m). Dashboards: dedicated -> Pools -> Throughput budgets (new panel).

Backward compatibility & rollout: controller is opt-in per Fleet by flipping dedicated.features.per_pool_budget to true. Default remains disabled for existing fleets. Rolling deploy strategy: start with internal canary fleet (5 clusters) -> gradual flag rollout across production pools -> enable automated telemetry-driven ramp.

Testing: unit tests for budget accounting, e2e integration test simulating sustained and bursty load shapes, and a small cluster-level soak run. Benchmarks show 1–3% CPU increase on controller nodes and no measurable increase in p99 latency for admission path.

Notes: Linear ENG-2189 covers follow-ups for multi-cluster budget reconciliation, and SUP-712 documents customer incident that motivated the change.

Hysteresis controller prevents rapid open/close admission cycles; configurable hold and thresholds.
